newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bonds tax to be clarified this week-finmin.
newsitem.headline: Greek bonds tax to be clarified this week-finmin.

text.p: Greece's finance ministry will clarify issues related to the taxation of government securities in the next few days, a high-level official at the finance ministry told Reuters.
"I believe, we will finalise everything in the next few days," said the official who declined to specify an exact date.

Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis told reporters on February 6 that his ministry would issue a bulletin clarifying bond-related taxation issues and containing specific examples last week but did not deliver.
Lingering doubts about tax issues have helped depress trading volume in the secondary bond market.
Greece slapped a 7.5 percent witholding tax on interest earned on government securities issued from January 1. Mutual funds and investment companies are taxed at 0.2 percent on their net assets.
It is not clear whether banks and corporations will be able to net the tax against other income taxes or carry it forward in case of losses.
The tax on T-bills is being collected upon issuance witheld at source. Two-year zero coupon bonds are taxed at maturity.
Taxes on coupon bonds and FRNs are collected on coupon payments dates.

A major issue is how foreign investors domiciled in countries having a full double taxation treaty with Greece will go about reclaiming taxes paid on securities and how long it is going to take them before they do so. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
